### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T11:33Z

Head-sha: 4b17fddc2b3d98fe665c91059e82e22ed8e573a6
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34685 (claim 6944611594, seat Premise corrected 6944554445, seat rulings 6945986942, dev report 6945937382).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34685`. The card's "Done when" items 2 and 3 are named on the card itself as the sibling cards' work (server card #34686 for single source, devx card #34687 for the runner repeat), so Fixes is the right keyword; see N1. No other issue number sits next to a closing verb.

**Scope vs claim.** Ten files, each inside the claim's file surface (widened by Premise corrected 6944554445): `skills/objectstack-ask/**` (SKILL.md, one eval file), `skills/README.md` and `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx` (generated), `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts` (one DISPLAY row), `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` (one CEILINGS row), `packages/create-objectstack/src/created-summary.test.ts`, the two pointer lines, the changeset. Nothing under `packages/mcp/**` or `packages/runtime/**` (routing A).

**Governed / tier.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34792`: 5 of 10 paths hit the register, governed (Tier H), 280 lines. Body carries `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` as the claim mandates. Seat L2 and os-zhuang follow this ACCEPT, including the new CEILINGS row (a pricing act the ratchet header reserves to the maintainer).

**Changeset.** `@objectstack/skills` patch, `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` (patch is right for none). `packages/spec/scripts/**` is not in spec's `files[]`; `create-objectstack` moved only a test; `content/docs/**` is not a package. Nothing else owed.

**Check-runs at 4b17fddc.** 70 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` + 8 shards, `Test UI` + 16 shards, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs`, `Scaffold with repo dist`.

**Re-run here at 4b17fddc.** `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: `58 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings`, bundle total 255871 (matches the body). `node scripts/check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs`: `1 justified exemption(s)`. The CEILINGS row's arithmetic (`ceil(5828 / 4) == 1457`) agrees with the ratchet's own reading.

**The skill against the served text (the area's ask).** I read `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` against `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts:265-291` row by row. Every served rule is in the skill with the same meaning: terms → `matches`; exact name/label/synonym (case, spacing, `_`/`-` aside), never similarity; one measure → `query_dataset`; several → ask with label, dataset, description, no pick; dimension alone is not an answer; no match → `query_records` / `aggregate_records`, labelled; `membersWithheld`; cite `provenance`, explain with `description`; data cannot answer → name what is missing, offer the computation, no assumed value; every figure from a tool answer. The one place they differ is the near-miss row (skill line 51), which the card's scope demands and the seat routed (B, 6944554445). It is wider than the served "no match: fall back", not contrary to any other served line, and it follows ADR-0149 D3 rule 1 (a near form "may be offered in rule 3's question, never acted on"). Single-loose-form behaviour (line 52 → fallback, lines 89-90 name the dataset) is the seat's Q1 A.

**Every name the skill uses exists.** Checked at this head: `terms`, `matches{term, member: measures.<n>|dimensions.<n>, matchedOn}`, `membersWithheld`, `object`, `partial` + `warning` (`packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`); `datasetName`, `selection.{measures, dimensions, runtimeFilter, dateGranularity, order, limit}` (`packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts` selection); `provenance` with dataset and measure labels, `truncated`, and `warning` as the narrowing statement on `query_dataset` (`DatasetProvenanceSchema`, `QueryDatasetOutputSchema`); `describe_object({ objectName })` fields with `options` (value + label) and `truncated: true` on `aggregate_records` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`). The claim "a call with `terms` already returns the whole catalogue; `terms` only adds `matches`" holds: `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts:410-440` builds every admitted entry and sets `matches` only when `terms` is defined. No `candidates` field is named anywhere in the skill or evals.

**Registration.** DISPLAY row, generated README and skills-reference regenerated (count 11 → 12), `created-summary.test.ts` SKILLS list matches the eleven `skills/objectstack-*` dirs. The test rewrite moves the symlink case from per-link lines to the collapsed farm line, as the old comment prescribed past COLLAPSE_AT; it still pins the property (each farm counts one entry per link and is sized as the links' own bytes, never their targets).

**Value density, read from the customer agent's seat.** 1457 tokens, loaded only on its trigger; the two pointer lines (23 and 28 tokens) sit in existing headroom. The description's trigger names the live-MCP setting and excludes metadata building and code queries, so a builder session should not load it. Acceptable for the job.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. Three eval cases assert words a correct reply does not carry.** The assertions were checked against each case's `expected_output` (meta description), not against an answer. Case 2 ("What is your reply?") requires `which one they mean`, `label`, `description`; a correct reply says "Which one do you mean?" and lists the labels themselves. Case 3 requires `compute nothing yet`, which a reply to the user does not say. Case 6 expects the reply in Chinese yet requires `membersWithheld` and `may not read`. The weekly runner (#34764) will grade these as written. Either reword them in this PR to tokens any right answer carries (the candidate labels, 财务汇总 / 无权 or similar), cheapest before the seat's L2 run, or the seat names #34789 (over-literal assertion review across `skills/*/evals/**`) as their carrier on the card. Seat's call.

### Notes
- N1. `Fixes #34685` closes the card while its "Done when" 2 (served text = skill) and 3 (runner repeat) are still open on #34686 PR2 and #34687. The card text assigns both there, so this is right; a one-line pointer on the card at landing would keep the trail.
- N2. Between this merge and #34686 PR2, the served `/mcp/skill` page and the skill differ on the near-miss row (the card asked not to leave two diverging texts). Routing A already queues PR2 behind this PR; no action here.
- N3. The generated sentence "plus process skills for how a project is delivered" (README and skills-reference) now also covers Ask, which is a procedure rather than a delivery process. The seat ruled `process` for this PR (Q2); a domain value is the epic seat's card if wanted.
- N4. The body's gate list shows two NOT MEASURED families locally (teardown self-test, dual-build); CI covers both on this head.

Next: seat L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, then os-zhuang (Tier H). A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

`git diff --stat 4b17fddc 63c79bc1`: one file, `skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json` (+13 / -13); `SKILL.md` and every other file unchanged, so the token readings and the CEILINGS row stand.

**S1 closed.** Re-read every case's assertions as a reply would meet them:
- Case 2: `Open Pipeline`, `Weighted Pipeline`, `Opportunities`, `Forecast`, `?`; forbids the tools and the machine names `open_amount` / `weighted_amount`. A correct ask-back carries all of these.
- Case 3: the three measure labels, their three dataset labels and `?`; forbids the tools and 非指标口径.
- Case 6: 财务汇总 and 毛利率, forbids 不存在. No English meta-words left in a case whose reply is Chinese.
- Cases 1, 4, 5 reworded the same way (1: `query_dataset`; 4: `describe_object`, `aggregate_records`, `priority`; 5: `weight`, `limit`).
- My own consistency pass at this head: every `must_contain` occurs in its `expected_output`, no `must_not_contain` does, ids 1-6 distinct.

The area's call to keep tool names in `must_not_contain` for cases 1-3 (so a reply that computes is still caught, at the cost of a false fail on a reply that names a tool it did not call) is a reasonable trade and stated in the body.

**Notes (no action owed on this PR).**
- N5. Case 4 is the card's "no metric, labelled fallback" branch, and it no longer asserts the label (非指标口径 left `must_contain` in this round). The skill's fallback label is therefore not string-checked by any case. #34687's `fallback-labelled` grader is the stronger check; #34789's assertion review can decide whether case 4 gets a language-neutral form.
- N6. Case 6's `不存在` can false-fail a correct reply phrased as 「并不代表毛利率不存在」. Same carrier, #34789.

Check-runs on this head were still pending when read; the area merges `origin/main` next and the seat's L2 reads that final head. A merge-only push needs no further L1 read beyond confirming the PR diff is unchanged; any content change owes one.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1a8bd8baddfa5ed29ab85e234ea12fc87a9fd292`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/README.md, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json, skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md + packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: yes

PR #34792 for card #34685, read at the head above (a merge of `origin/main` 3bbda33b into 63c79bc1; the net diff against `main` is ten files). Inputs: the card body and all nine comments, the PR body and its comments, the net diff, and the head's check-runs. Read to judge, not reviewed: ADR-0149 on `main` (D1 to D4, M2), `packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts` (the selection schema), `packages/services/service-analytics/src/{dataset-tools,dataset-term-matcher,analytics-service}.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` and `mcp-http-tools.ts`, and the rulings 6940528935 (#34659), F1 B (#34691, record 6943149235), 6945986942 (#34685) and 6946563869 (#34720).

Remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, not judged here: `packages/create-objectstack/src/created-summary.test.ts`, `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx` (generated), `.changeset/34685-ask-data-skill.md` (read for ② only).

`Security-touching: yes` is meant. Two hunks of `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` teach permission behaviour the path name does not show: the `membersWithheld` row (what to tell a user about members they may not read) and the `warning` sentence in step 3 (an agent's narrowed read is repeated to the user). The PR also adds `skills/**` files, so it is Tier H either way.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A twelfth published skill, `objectstack-ask`, joins `@objectstack/skills`.** Right. The card's scope asks for one new skill whose reader is an MCP client; the name is the card's starting text. Accept-set: nothing that parsed before is refused; no schema, tool or served text moves.
- **Catalog index.** `skills/README.md` gains one generated row and the generated guide counts 12. Right: the row's text is the frontmatter description's first sentence, and the `DISPLAY` row that orders it is in this diff.
- **Trigger surface.** The description triggers on a user asking for a number, ranking, breakdown, trend or list, in any language, and excludes metadata building and code queries. Right against the card's scope line ("not a file glob").
- **Token price.** One new `CEILINGS` row, 1457, zero headroom; no existing row moves. Arithmetic re-derived from the blobs: `SKILL.md` is 5848 bytes, its stamp line 20, `ceil(5828 / 4) = 1457`. `objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is 25477 bytes less a 20-byte stamp, 6365 against 6801; `objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md` is 9168 bytes, 2292 against 2357. Right.
- **`metadata.domain: process`, `compatibility: ... @objectstack/mcp 18.x`.** Right: the seat ruled `process` for this PR (6945986942, Q2), and the README's own table lets a `process` skill name the tooling it needs.
- **No `candidates` field is named** in the skill or the evals (the word "candidate" appears only as prose for the measures offered in a question). Right while #34761 and #34763 are open.
- **Gate verdicts on this head are not all in.** Read at 2026-11-17T11:56Z: 23 check-runs `success`, 11 `skipped`, 34 `in_progress`, none failed. Completed green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Scaffold with repo dist, Type Check · source gates, and seven of the eight Lint jobs (CI, release & engine gates; ESLint; docs & code guards; repo & tooling gates; the two scoped lookups; tooling self-tests). Still running: Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, · debt ledger and · workspace. The derived judgments above are read from the tree; the running jobs still owe their answer, and this PASS does not answer for them.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` at `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on both the PR body and the changeset. Right. The diff publishes teaching text only: one added skill directory and two pointer lines. No schema, no tool input or output, no metadata key, so no conversion is owed and clause ② does not apply. `packages/spec/scripts/**` and the ratchet script are repo tooling and ship in no package; `create-objectstack` moved a test file only. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

Clause-②: no. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6945937382, deviations:
1. "The answer in hand is already the catalogue" (no second `list_datasets` call on a zero-match). Confirmed in the code: `listDatasets` pushes every admitted entry with all admitted members and sets `matches` only when `terms` is defined (`dataset-tools.ts`, the `if (terms !== undefined) entry.matches = ...` line). Accepted; the seat accepted it too (6945986942).
2. Terms are sent as written, no client-side translation. Accepted: it follows D3 rule 1 and agrees with ruling 6946563869 (a bundle label matches in the caller's locale only; a cross-locale word is an authored synonym). The skill promises no cross-locale match anywhere.
3. `created-summary.test.ts` rewrite. Outside ④; the lane seat's ACCEPT.
4. The `CEILINGS` row is a maintainer-only pricing act. Answered below under the ratchet file: this record does not stand in for that word; the Tier H approval does.
5, 6. PR body layout and trailer. Not contract matters.

Dev report 6945937382, open questions:
- Q1, one loose form on a zero-match: ruled A by the seat (6945986942). The skill conforms: that case falls to the fifth table row (step 4), and step 4's last bullet names the dataset when the fallback object is its `object`. No row lets a loose form select a measure.
- Q2, `metadata.domain`: ruled `process` (same record).

Dev report 6947110992, open question: keep tool names in `must_not_contain` for cases 1 to 3. Answered A, keep. Without them cases 2 and 3 cannot catch a reply that computes; the false fail on a reply that names the tool it did not call is stated in the PR body and has a carrier, #34789.

Out-of-scope findings: the served text has no near-miss row (carrier #34686); no committed gate checks the `objectstack-*` eval files' self-consistency (carrier #34789). Both stand as filed; neither is this PR's to fix.

SQL push-down: no code path in the diff. The skill's own teaching is on the right side of Prime Directive 5: `aggregate_records` for a count, sum, average or breakdown, never paging `query_records` to add rows up.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md`**, sentence by sentence against ADR-0149 and the rulings.

Holds:
- Step 1. Lifting the words and sending them as `terms` is D2's input and D3's "the model still decides what the question's terms are". "A word matches only when it equals a member's name, label or synonym (case, spacing, `_` and `-` aside), never by similarity" is D3 rule 1 and the matcher's behaviour. "No `list_datasets` among your tools ... go to step 4" is D2's graceful degradation.
- Step 2, row 1 (one measure match, compute) is rule 2. Row 3 (dimension only) is rule 5, including its "or asks". Row 5 (no match, no several readings: fall back and say so) is rule 4 and M2 A.
- Step 2, row 4 (the near-miss ask-back) goes beyond rule 4 as it reads on `main`, and is ruled: the E2 premise in 6940528935 names exactly this skill-only branch, F1 B re-ruled the server half, and seat routing B (6944554445) keeps the catalogue-read row until the `candidates` cards land. It never selects, which is the limit rule 1's parenthetical sets. It promises no `candidates` field.
- Step 3. Every selection key exists on `DatasetSelectionSchema` (`measures`, `dimensions`, `runtimeFilter`, `dateGranularity`, `order`, `limit`); `provenance`, `truncated` and `warning` are on `QueryDatasetOutputSchema` with the meanings given; the citation form is D3 rule 2's own example.
- Step 4. The label line and the "name the dataset and its measures" line are rule 4 and M2's recommended practice; `truncated: true` on `aggregate_records` and `describe_object({ objectName })` with `options` exist as taught.
- Steps 5 and 6 say what the served text says (`skill-md.ts`, the "When the data cannot answer" entry).
- `partial` / `warning` on the `list_datasets` answer are as `ListDatasetsOutputSchema` declares them.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — Step 2, row 2 drops D3 rule 3's "answer to the word". The row reads "Several measures match (two members, or one word in two datasets) → ask the user which one they mean". Rule 3 is per word: "More than one hit (two datasets, or two members, answer to the word)", and the `list_datasets` tool description on `main` keeps those words. As written, the "one word" qualifier binds only the two-datasets arm, so a question that names two metrics ("营收和赢单率", "revenue and win rate by stage"), where each word has exactly one hit and rule 2 says each wins, lands on this row and is taught as an ask-back. Inside one dataset the D1 validation refuses two members that answer to one word, so in practice the "two members" arm fires almost only on that multi-metric case. The effect is a wrong question, never a wrong number, which is why it is not a must-fix; it also cuts against the E2 premise's second half (no ask-back where each word has one match). Fix: make rows 1 and 2 per word (for example "Each word matches one measure" / "One word matches several measures, in one dataset or in two"). No eval case covers a two-metric question; one would pin it.

S2 (should-fix) — the `membersWithheld` row states more than the flag says. The skill: "Say that it has measures you may not read." The flag is set when ANY member was withheld, a dimension included: `admitDatasetCatalogEntry` raises `withheld` in the same `judge` call for the dimensions loop and the measures loop (`analytics-service.ts`), the schema describes it as "a member was left out", and the tool description says "some members exist that this caller may not see". On a dataset where only a grouping field is unreadable, the skill has the client tell the user that measures exist which they may not see, which is a false statement about permissions. Eval case 6 bakes the same reading in ("it has measures this user may not read, so the reply says exactly that"). Fix: "members (measures or groupings) you may not read; the metric asked for may be among them", and the same word in case 6's `expected_output`. The served text on `main` carries the same wording; that copy is #34686's to render from this skill, so fixing it here fixes both.

Both fixes change `SKILL.md`'s byte count: the `CEILINGS` row is re-measured in the same push and stays pinned at the measurement.

Nits (no action owed on this head; prose faces only, or a carrier):
- N1. The single-loose-form case (seat ruling Q1 A) is taught only by elimination: it is whatever row 4 does not catch. The opening sentence "a governed metric ... outranks a number you work out yourself" pulls the other way. One clause on row 5 ("one near form is not a match either") would say it outright. No eval pins it; #34687's graders are the carrier.
- N2. Row 3 and row 5 overlap when a grouping word equals some dataset's dimension and the measure word matches nothing (a ticket question "by priority" beside a sales dataset with a `priority` dimension): row 3 asks, row 5 falls back. ADR-0149 rule 5 has the same "or asks", so this is the ADR's own latitude, to be settled by #34687's numbers.
- N3. A list question ("列出…") is in the trigger, has no measure, and so always reaches step 4, where the answer opens with the not-a-governed-metric line. Harmless, slightly odd on a plain record list.
- N4. The generated sentence "plus process skills for how a project is delivered" and the README's "delivery-process skill" now cover a skill that is not a delivery process. Ruled `process` for this PR; a domain value is the epic seat's card.

**`skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json`.** Six cases, ids 1 to 6, one per branch the card lists (one match, several matches, near-miss, no metric, data cannot answer, `membersWithheld`). Every `must_contain` entry (19) occurs in its case's `expected_output`; no `must_not_contain` entry (14) does. Each `expected_output` agrees with the skill row it exercises: case 1 with rows 1 and step 3; case 2 with row 2 and "show labels, not machine names"; case 3 with row 4 and "the reply is the question alone"; case 4 with row 5 and step 4; case 5 with step 5; case 6 with the withheld row, subject to S2. Case 4 no longer string-checks the fallback label and case 6's `不存在` can false-fail a negated sentence; both were noted by L1 (N5, N6) with #34789 as carrier, and I agree with that placing.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`** and **`skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md`.** One pointer line each, the two the seat's premise correction assigned to this card. Both are true of the tree (the MCP section publishes the tools; `aggregate_records` is the MCP-side name) and both send the right reader away: the builder stays, the connected client goes to `objectstack-ask`. Both sit inside existing headroom.

**`skills/README.md`.** One generated row inside the `BEGIN GENERATED` block, byte-for-byte the description's first sentence. Holds; see N4.

**`packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts`** (implementing). One `DISPLAY` row, `objectstack-ask` / `Ask`, placed before `objectui`. It agrees with the frontmatter it reads: the folded description splits at "Use when" and "Do not use" as the parser expects, and `domain` and `tags` parse from the `metadata:` map. Holds.

**`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`** (implementing). The new row is governed rules text inside a gate, so it is judged, sentence by sentence:
- "an INITIAL measurement of the new file on the PR that adds it, pinned AT it — zero headroom, on the same terms as the objectui rows above": true, and the audit formula in the comment reproduces (5848 less the 20-byte stamp line, 1457).
- "Its evals are unpriced (population 1b)": true; no row is added on the eval path, which the gate would red.
- "No existing row moves": true, re-derived above.
- "Adding the row is the pricing act the header reserves to the maintainer; the PR that adds it is Tier H and lands only on the maintainer's approval": this matches the gate's own unpriced-file message and the objectui precedent's wording. It is a statement of what is owed, not a claim that it was given. This record does not give it: the row lands on os-zhuang's approval of this PR and on nothing else.
- The heading cites ruling 6940528935 as "(D5 A)". The record is the right one; the new skill itself rests on that record's word 2 and the card's filing gate, D5 A being the "server points to the local skills package" letter. Close enough to find; not a finding.
- The 10402 principle (no growth for a small feature) is not in play: this is a ruled new skill, and its two pointer lines cost 23 and 28 tokens inside headroom.

No must-fix. Two should-fix, S1 and S2, open on this head; their fix earns a delta review, and the delta record names them by id.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34685-ask-data-skill`
